title: LoadBalancer IPs don't seem to be being advertised (pod cidr works)
body: I have a Plex LoadBalancer service with external IP 10.100.198.10 from a CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool, but FRR and OPNsense only receive the pod CIDR routes. The LoadBalancer pool routes do not appear in received routes and are not being filtered. I have tried different IP-pool selectors, while kubectl still shows the external IP assigned to the service. My CiliumBGPPeeringPolicy and LoadBalancer IP-pool configuration are included.

symptoms_visible: FRR and OPNsense receive the pod CIDR routes, but I cannot see any route for the LoadBalancer IP even though kubectl shows 10.100.198.10 assigned to the Plex service.
N0.label: N0 LoadBalancer route absent

symptoms_visible: After adding the service selector, I see the LoadBalancer IP appear and get advertised upstream, but it repeatedly changes back to <pending> and the route is added and removed.
If I delete the old bgp-config ConfigMap, Cilium stops working and asks for that configuration to be applied again.
N1_x.label: N1_x selector-only attempt leaves route flapping

symptoms_visible: The external IP continues alternating between an assigned address and <pending>.
My Cilium logs include a withdrawal for 10.100.198.10/32 and an 'assigned IP not allowed by config' message from bgp-speaker.
N2.label: N2 flapping configuration and logs collected

symptoms_visible: The LoadBalancer route is still being added and withdrawn with my current Cilium installation.
N3.label: N3 Helm BGP mode identified

symptoms_visible: After the Helm upgrade, the upstream BGP table shows the LoadBalancer route 10.12.248.1/32 advertised from my Cilium nodes.
N_terminal.label: terminal LoadBalancer route advertised

solution.intent: Add a serviceSelector to the CiliumBGPPeeringPolicy that matches the LoadBalancer service so its virtual IP is eligible for advertisement.
solution.concrete_example: Label the service, for example color=red, and add serviceSelector.matchLabels.color: red to the virtual router in the CiliumBGPPeeringPolicy.

edges.comment: Opening and c0-c10, all on the original reporter's cluster: participant1 suggested serviceSelector, and the reporter's later policy output shows color:red was applied. It made the VIP eligible and produced advertisements, but did not resolve the issue because the IP and route then repeatedly appeared and disappeared.

question_patterns: Can you share the current peering policy, IP-pool objects, and Cilium agent logs while the route is being added and removed?
What do kubectl and the Cilium logs show at the moment the external IP changes back to pending?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My current policy has serviceSelector.matchLabels.color: red, and my pools are active and non-conflicting. While it flaps, kubectl alternates between the assigned external IP and <pending>. The logs show withdrawals="[10.100.198.10/32]" and also say `op setBalancer error assigned IP not allowed by config msg IP allocated by controller not allowed by config` with subsys=bgp-speaker.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The IP remains assigned and the Cilium logs contain no withdrawals or bgp-speaker errors; only the upstream router fails to install the consistently advertised route.
The same withdrawal and assigned-IP error occur for a different address from the same LoadBalancer pool.

edges.comment: Reporter c5-c10: these are raw outputs from the original reporter's cluster. The answer preserves the observed policy, pool status, withdrawal, and bgp-speaker error without placing the controller-mode conclusion in the user's mouth.

question_patterns: How was Cilium installed? Please share the exact Helm command or current BGP-related Helm values.
Can you show the Cilium version and the BGP settings used by your Helm installation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I installed Cilium 1.15.4 with `--set bgp.enabled=true --set bgp.announce.loadbalancerIP=true`; I did not set `bgpControlPlane.enabled=true`. The command was `helm install cilium cilium/cilium --version 1.15.4 --namespace kube-system --set global.mtu=1450 --set tunnel=wireguard --set kubeProxyReplacement=strict --set bgp.enabled=true --set bgp.announce.loadbalancerIP=true --set k8sServiceHost=10.12.100.10 --set k8sServicePort=6443`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My current Helm values already have bgpControlPlane.enabled=true and bgp.enabled=false, and the agents were restarted with those values before the flapping began.
The same BGP flags were used with another Cilium 1.15 patch release.

edges.comment: Reporter c11: exact installation command from the original reporter. The raw Helm flags are user-provided evidence; recognizing that they select the legacy mode while the reporter is configuring control-plane CRDs is engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: Use the CRD-based BGP control plane consistently: keep the matching serviceSelector, enable the BGP control plane, disable the legacy BGP mode, restart through the Helm upgrade, and verify the LoadBalancer route upstream.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade with the reporter's working mode selection, including `--set bgpControlPlane.enabled=true --set bgp.enabled=false`, while retaining a serviceSelector that matches the LoadBalancer service. Then check the upstream BGP table for the service /32.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw Helm flags and logs from both the BGP control-plane path and bgp-speaker. Concluding that the deployment was mixing the legacy BGP setup with CRD-based control-plane configuration, and therefore should run only the latter, is the diagnostic inference.

edges.comment: Reporter c11-c13 on the original deployment: the reporter changed the Helm settings to bgpControlPlane.enabled=true and bgp.enabled=false, said the result looked better, and posted an upstream BGP table containing 10.12.248.1/32. Later BGPv2 reports from other participants describe a separate multi-instance problem and are intentionally excluded from this causal chain.

solution.intent: Correct the complete BGP setup immediately by selecting the CRD-based BGP control plane instead of the legacy mode and by adding a serviceSelector matching the LoadBalancer service.
solution.concrete_example: Add a serviceSelector matching the LoadBalancer service, then upgrade Cilium with `bgpControlPlane.enabled=true` and `bgp.enabled=false`. Restart the agents through the upgrade and verify that the service /32 appears in the upstream received routes.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the original reporter's eventual resolution. It permits a correct first response while explicitly recording that it skips the selector-only aftermath, logs, old ConfigMap behavior, and exact Helm-install evidence gathered in c4-c11.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both parts of the original reporter's configuration problem: the LoadBalancer service needs to match a serviceSelector for BGP advertisement, and the CRD-based BGP policy must be used with the BGP control plane enabled rather than the legacy BGP mode.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: adding the selector made the route appear but flap, logs showed route withdrawals and a bgp-speaker allocation error, and the Helm command enabled legacy BGP without enabling the BGP control plane.
Must not present adding serviceSelector alone as the complete fix, because that attempt left the external IP alternating with <pending> and repeatedly added and removed the route.
Must not treat changing the LoadBalancer pool from blocks to cidrs as the accepted resolution; the reporter continued using blocks and obtained an advertised route after correcting the BGP mode.
Must have the reporter verify that the LoadBalancer /32 appears in the upstream BGP table after reconfiguration before declaring the original no-advertisement issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable homelab Kubernetes operator who can edit Cilium CRDs and Helm values, inspect FRR and OPNsense routing tables, collect kubectl output, and read Cilium debug logs, but is uncertain about the distinction between Cilium's legacy and CRD-based BGP modes.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal, exploratory, and cooperative; shares extensive raw configuration and logs, tests suggestions independently, and openly states uncertainty while debugging.
